program: Child behavioral health, family support, training, research and Camp SOAR

acceptance.evidence: docs/geography-discovery/chicago-crt-alpha-acceptance.md: conditional research alpha only; donor HOLD

priceScope: Conditional whole-recipient recognized-resource scenario; donor HOLD; only short-horizon aligned trauma-care benefit quantified

what: CRT provides child behavioral-health evaluations and therapy through its clinic and community partners.
Its broader portfolio includes family support, training, research and Camp SOAR.
Most reported reach combines children and families and does not establish unique completed therapy courses.
strengths: Original filings and audits establish the recipient and reconcile resource costs.
Actual community sites and named therapy approaches support a plausible access mechanism.
Current operating sites and public grant records corroborate continued program activity.
reservations: Mixed reach is not unique treatment starts or completions; local causal outcomes are unverified.
New grants require an updated funding-gap and capacity assessment.
The conditional QALY scenario omits longer-term and nontherapy net health.

sections.what:
Children's Research Triangle (CRT), EIN 36-4236142, provides child behavioral-health assessment and therapy, family support, professional training, research, and Camp SOAR. An ordinary gift supports this whole recipient. The official donation page names this EIN and links a donation form; no transaction was made. [Donate](https://childrensresearchtriangle.org/donate/)

Community therapists work at schools and social-service sites in Chicago, Evanston and Dolton, as well as the Loop clinic and telehealth. These are actual service anchors in Cook County, not merely headquarters evidence. The edition uses the Chicago-Naperville-Elgin MSA under OMB-23-01 (21 July 2023); residence-level attribution remains unverified. [Sites](https://childrensresearchtriangle.org/clinical-services/community-partners/)

Retain all assessment, clinical, camp, training, research, administration and fundraising costs. The audit identifies a separate for-profit affiliate, CRT Medical PC, with shared office/subcontract arrangements; this report does not merge that entity or attribute its services automatically.
sections.monitoring:
The 2024 annual report gives 1,368 children and families served, 786 people trained and 23 partners. Its 87% trauma-symptom improvement and 85% behavioral/emotional improvement figures lack denominators, attrition, timing, effect sizes and a comparison group. They are recipient monitoring claims, not causal recovery rates. [2024 report, printed p. 2](https://childrensresearchtriangle.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/CRT-2024-Annual-Report-1.pdf)

The report titled Impact Report 2025 gives 1,365 children/families, 805 trainees and 15 partners, alongside 86% trauma-symptom and 84% functioning improvement. Its camp section reports 96 campers and 130+ volunteer counselors/staff. The later HHS award narrative instead calls 1,166 people clients in 2025. Definitions are unreconciled; none is verified unique trauma-treatment starts or completions. Projected grant treatment of 70 children/caregivers annually is a target, not observed delivery. [2025 impact](https://childrensresearchtriangle.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/2026-Impact-Report-8.5-x-11-in-1.pdf) [Award](https://taggs.hhs.gov/Detail/AwardDetail?arg_AwardNum=H79SM091564&arg_ProgOfficeCode=80)

Request deidentified annual cohorts by residence, diagnosis, modality, first start, adequate dose, completion, follow-up and alternative treatment. Include missing outcomes and harms.
sections.qualitative:
School/community delivery and no-cost partner-site care offer a plausible way to reduce access barriers. CRT lists TF-CBT, CPP, SPARCS, PCIT, Theraplay, EMDR and parenting interventions; the mix is not quantified. [Therapy](https://childrensresearchtriangle.org/clinical-services/therapy/)

A CRT-affiliated randomized trial compared 40 treated with 38 control children with FAS/ARND and found improvements in executive functioning and emotional problem solving. That supports one historical intervention, not contemporary trauma-care QALYs or the ordinary gift. Its registry distinguishes standard referrals in controls; planned follow-up is not evidence of observed persistence. [Wells et al.](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22251828/) [Registration](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT00164346)

External therapy evidence supports plausible benefit but weakens any automatic symptom-to-QALY bridge. A Norwegian TF-CBT randomized economic evaluation found no significant QALY difference versus usual therapy, despite a favorable cost-effectiveness probability. [Aas et al.](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29877724/)

Caregiver welfare, evaluations, research, training, crisis services, school violence prevention and camp respite may help or harm. Their net health H is unmeasured; H=0 is a modeling omission, not no value. Avoid double counting child, parent and partner gains. Family time, volunteer labor and space also consume resources.
sections.cost:
The illustrative central scenario uses $3,523,321 of whole-recipient FY2024 gross recognized resources. Its short-horizon therapy-only pathway gives approximately 0.039 Chicago-MSA QALYs, implying about $913 million per 10 QALYs. This is not an observed return, expected-value recommendation, restricted therapy price or scalable donation tranche. Donor readiness: HOLD.

Q_all = b × (N × s × q × t × a + H); Q_MSA = g × Q_all; price10 = 10 × (C+K)/Q_MSA only for positive Q_MSA. N=1,368 is mixed reported reach; s=.1 is the assumed number of eligible distinct trauma-treatment starts per reported reach unit. It combines deduplication, child-only scope, diagnosis, age and modality alignment. It is not observed 10% eligibility. t=.25 transports the external trial pathway, including local fidelity/completion differences; a=.5 removes equivalent timely alternative care; b=.25 is a hypothetical proportional gift-to-capacity response; g=.95 is a resident-health judgment. Unknown K and signed H are conditionally zero.

The external q=.0095 is the adjusted, imputed difference in QALYs over an 11-week UK trial of 29 children aged 8–17 with PTSD after a recent single event. It used SDQ mapped to CHU-9D. This is CT-PTSD, not CRT's complete modality mix; chronic trauma and younger children make transfer especially uncertain. The trial already includes noncompletion through imputation: no second completion multiplier is applied. We credit nothing after 11 weeks in the central scenario; this deliberately excludes possible later benefit. A separate sensitivity uses the paper's three-year modeled gain .0577 (about $150 million per 10 QALYs under other central assumptions); this is not observed long-term follow-up and is excluded from the central estimate. [Shearer et al., Table 4](https://acamh.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/jcpp.12851)

The historical mixed denominator and current gifts are linked only by a stable-productivity assumption. Cases vary that assumption, zero finance/clinical effect/eligible reach, equivalent alternative treatment, geography, resource costs and signed other-portfolio health. Values are judgment stress tests, not confidence bounds or a posterior distribution.
sections.funding:
Original FY2022–24 Form 990 Part IX expense is $2,957,499, $3,303,788 and $3,415,329. Adding direct event expense of $78,325, $136,556 and $107,992 yields comparable gross recorded resources of $3,035,824, $3,440,344 and $3,523,321 (mean $3,333,163). In 2024, audited expense is $3,521,499; Schedule D adds $1,822 investment expense netted in the audit and removes direct events to reach Part IX. Thus the model keeps that investment resource cost; it does not confuse the audit total with Part IX. [2022 return](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/full_text/202312939349301511/IRS990) [2023 return](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/full_text/202403129349303570/IRS990) [2024 return](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/full_text/202543169349304119/IRS990) [Schedule D](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/full_text/202543169349304119/IRS990ScheduleD)

All three original audits were inspected. FY2024 cash was $614,925 and net assets $776,629, including a $125,000 board reserve. The $709,579 lease liability explains most liabilities; it is not an ordinary cash borrowing. The audit's financial assets available within one year were $630,484 and the undrawn credit line $100,000. These are dated balances, not present liquidity. Opinion was unmodified; no current audit findings were listed. Volunteer/partner resources are not fully valued. [2024 audit](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/display_audit/2024-12-GSAFAC-0000381225)

The 2025 impact appeal projects a 2026 gap above $300,000 and federal support reaching zero by end-2026. Subsequent evidence prevents treating that appeal as current room: HHS records a new $499,896 action on 31 August 2026, performance period 30 September 2026–29 September 2031; Impact Grants Chicago confirms a 2026 $100,000 award, and Invest for Kids lists CRT among current beneficiaries. Award periods/restrictions differ; do not simply subtract awards from the old gap or assume five years are fully funded. [HHS](https://taggs.hhs.gov/Detail/AwardDetail?arg_AwardNum=H79SM091564&arg_ProgOfficeCode=80) [Impact Grants](https://www.impactgrantschicago.org/all-grant-recipients/) [Invest for Kids](https://investforkidschicago.org/beneficiary-category/current-year/)

Before a recommendation, reconcile current cash, grant restrictions/renewals, remaining commitments and staffing capacity to a priced incremental plan, alongside unique local outcomes and a validated utility/duration bridge. The $3,000-per-child implication of the old appeal is not used as a marginal cost.

model.costScope: Full legal recipient FY2024 gross recorded resources C; all programs, admin, direct event and investment expenses retained. Add unknown net unrecognized K. Separate for-profit CRT Medical PC not consolidated.
model.geographicAttribution: Chicago-Naperville-Elgin MSA, OMB-23-01-2023-07-21; actual Cook County sites observed. g=.95 is an unverified resident-health fraction.
model.formula: Q_all=b*(N*s*q*t*a+H); Q_MSA=g*Q_all; price10=10*(C+K)/Q_MSA only if Q_MSA>0. q is 11-week trial QALY gain; no additional duration or completion multiplier.
model.counterfactual: Without the extra ordinary gift, current grants, existing clinical services, reserves and other providers remain. Capacity response b captures replacement or expansion; a removes equivalent timely care. Waitlist/usual services remain for credited patients, as in external trial.
model.attribution: s converts mixed reach into distinct aligned child course starts; t transports clinical pathway including fidelity/completion. b financial additionality and a alternative treatment differ but are correlated. No measured recipient causal health is claimed.
model.uncertainty: Very weak confidence; hypothetical scenarios, not expected value, confidence intervals or donor-ready estimates. Unknown K and H conditionally zero; no proof of linear scalability. Short horizon excludes possible lasting benefit.
model.nativeOutcomes: Unique client starts and adequate therapy dose/completion, symptoms and functioning, family stress, evaluation follow-through, camp respite; reported reach and percentages cannot establish these causal outcomes.

inputs.name: C
inputs.unit: USD whole-recipient gross recognized FY2024 resources
inputs.rationale: Part IX 3,415,329 plus 107,992 direct events. Equals audit expense 3,521,499 plus 1,822 investment fee netted there; includes all programs/admin/fundraising, not a current marginal price.

inputs.name: N
inputs.rationale: Not known unique children, treatment starts or completions. No automatic assignment of one unit to one treated child.

inputs.name: s
inputs.unit: eligible distinct trial-like child course starts per reported reach unit
inputs.rationale: Assumes 10 per 100 heterogeneous reach units become aligned starts after deduplication, child-only scope, age/diagnosis/modality filters. Actual fraction unknown; 2.5–30% stress tests. Clinical mix and broad evaluation/training portfolio motivate a small fraction, not empirical calibration.

inputs.name: q
inputs.unit: incremental QALY per child assigned over 11 weeks in external trial
inputs.rationale: Adjusted imputed Table 4 estimate in 29-person UK CT-PTSD study; mapped SDQ utility. This is a noisy external effect, not a CRT observation. No persistence after trial is credited.

inputs.name: t
inputs.rationale: Quarter external effect for different modality, chronic/repeated trauma, age/severity, fidelity and local completion. Trial imputation already includes missing follow-up; no extra completion factor. Zero and negative clinical cases retained.

inputs.name: a
inputs.unit: fraction lacking equally effective timely alternative care
inputs.rationale: Half would obtain equivalent care otherwise; waitlist/usual services remain for credited half. Actual alternatives unobserved.

inputs.name: b
inputs.unit: capacity response to small proportional unrestricted-resource increase
inputs.rationale: Quarter proportional response; not fraction of a gift earmarked for therapy. Current grants, reserves and staff constraints make response unknown. New award invalidates reliance on old gap alone. Zero case essential.

inputs.name: g
inputs.unit: fraction of modeled net health in pinned Chicago MSA
inputs.rationale: Actual Chicago/Evanston/Dolton service sites and audit primary metro service support high share; no client residence roster. Applied to health, not headquarters allocation.

inputs.name: K
inputs.unit: USD net unrecognized partner/volunteer resource cost
inputs.rationale: Conditional zero; partner space and camp volunteer labor unvalued. 25% add-on is illustrative, not measured. Do not double count paid labor/leases already in C.

inputs.name: H
inputs.unit: signed non-modeled portfolio QALYs before b and g
inputs.rationale: Conditional zero for caregiver, camp, evaluation, research, training, crisis and prevention net outcomes. Signed +/-1 are stress tests, not observations; remove overlaps before adding.

sensitivity: Zero finance, clinical effect, eligible starts and complete alternative care each remove quantified benefits.
Signed clinical and other-portfolio cases may imply net harm; never display a positive price for nonpositive QALYs.
Mixed reach, eligibility, transfer and gift response dominate; no probability distribution is validated.
No benefit after eleven weeks in central model; explicitly incomplete lifetime and whole-portfolio valuation.
New 2026 grants make stable historical funding response particularly uncertain.

Recipient comparison-based health outcomes, adverse events, utility mapping and persistence.
